reason: The passage explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's care for His people through multiple elements: (1) God 'dealt well with the midwives' (וַיֵּיטֶב אֱלֹהִים לַמְיַלְּדֹת) as a reward for fearing Him and refusing to participate in genocide; (2) God established households for the midwives (וַיַּעַשׂ לָהֶם בָּתִּים), a blessing for their faithfulness; (3) The Hebrew people multiplied and became very strong (וַיִּרֶב הָעָם וַיַּעַצְמוּ מְאֹד) as a result of God's favor toward those who fear Him. The passage frames God's care as operative through blessing those who are faithful to Him, protecting His people from Pharaoh's genocidal decree indirectly through divine reward and multiplication.
